goal: Detect homologous coding sequences despite synonymous nucleotide differences while preserving comprehensive-reference competition and per-read evidence
constraints: Same core_nt snapshot and original nucleotide accession/taxonomy provenance
Original per-read results, no verdict extrapolation
Freeze evaluation inputs before outcome-based tuning

candidates.mechanism: Translate query and reference in six frames during search
advantages: No new reference-content choice or index build
limitations: Standard code1 does not model frameshifts or all genetic codes

advantages: Tolerates some third-position changes without full translation
limitations: Nucleotide extension and scoring still penalize synonymous substitutions
Third-position pattern does not represent all synonymous codons

candidates.status: Evaluate retrospective routing only after full-search evidence
candidates.mechanism: Run inexpensive search first, spend translated-search work on selected queries
limitations: Strong nucleotide viral hit does not prove absence of a stronger translated nonviral competitor
If only no-hit reads advance, measure all changed assignments missed on confident reads
Savings may be small if repeated reference scan dominates

candidates.status: Reserve for disagreements showing the need

required_controls: Do not claim score or Evalue parity; fixture differs despite identical aligned sequence
Normalize per-frame query coordinates and query coverage back to original nucleotide read
Combine frames before per-read near-best taxonomy

capacity_math.formula: six frames / three bases per amino acid = about two amino-acid letters per nucleotide; excludes headers, maps, compression, ORF filtering, index and temporary files
capacity_math.decision: Do not start a multi-terabyte translation/index build before measuring direct search and estimating amortization

comparison_axes: Per-read new/lost taxonomic evidence and near-best competitors
CPU time, wall time, peak memory and allocated cost
Index build and storage, amortized across realistic repeated use
Synonymous substitutions, nonsynonymous substitutions, frameshift and repeat failure mechanisms

decision_rules.same_reference: Derived indexes must represent the full original snapshot and preserve every accession/taxon mapping; a translated index changes representation, not chosen reference content. Explicitly report any ORF or length exclusions.
decision_rules.uncertain_query_cascade: Measure retrospective routing against completed full-search outputs. Never assume a strong nucleotide viral hit has no translated competing match.
decision_rules.break_even: For R repeated batches, compare direct_cost(R) with index_build_cost + R*indexed_search_cost + retained_index_storage_cost. Fit only within measured batch-size range; report fixed reference scan and marginal query work separately.
decision_rules.evidence_quality: Inspect strong disagreements at sequence/codon level and retain weak significance results separately. Absence of a translated hit is not proof a nucleotide hit is false; short or noncoding reads can behave differently.
decision_rules.batching: Shared-query alignment and assignment parity across3/24/96panels is an empirical check, not assumed.
decision_rules.false_positive_check: If new weak or low-complexity matches drive differences, use deterministic composition-preserving shuffled controls before claiming increased sensitivity. No truth-label accuracy claim from these observational reads.
